extracted.intended_audience: national IP offices, statisticians, policy analysts, WIPO member state authorities and researchers working with GI and publishing statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, definitions and metrics for collecting, classifying and reporting data on geographical indications (GIs) in force and publishing‑industry statistics (revenue, titles, legal deposits, ISBNs) for submission to WIPO and for comparative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical indications in force (count)
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of GIs in force within a territory (national or regional) in a given year (e.g., 'GIs in force in 2021').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EU regional system GIs are in force in every member state but counted once (to minimize double counting). Counts include GIs in force via international agreements (e.g., Lisbon System) where applicable. Data reported are partial/incomplete and should be interpreted with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal means of protection (classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs are classified by the legal means through which they are protected: sui generis systems, trademarks (including certification and collective marks), other national legal means, regional systems, and international agreements (including the Lisbon and Madrid Systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the EU regional system is itself sui generis, GIs in force via the EU are reported under the regional system category rather than the sui generis category. Lisbon System data reported here refer to foreign GIs and appellations of origin in force based on the Lisbon System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of GIs protected via trademark system (reporting difficulty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying GIs protected via the trademark system (certification and collective marks) is extremely time consuming and requires extensive manual intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this reason a number of authorities were unable to report on GIs protected via the trademark system; lack of reporting may reflect either non-use of trademark system for GIs or difficulty separating GIs from other trademarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: GIs by source (national vs foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of GIs in force that are national versus foreign (i.e., originating domestically or coming from abroad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: national GI share ranged from 2.2% (UK) to 100% (Argentina) in the reported sample. Use this metric to describe the domestic/foreign composition of GIs in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: GIs by product category
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of GIs in force by product category (Wines and spirits; Agricultural products and foodstuffs; Handicrafts; Others; Services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Wines and spirits accounted for 51% globally (of the sample); note that data coverage differs by country (China's 2021 product category data unavailable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellations of origin and GIs via Lisbon System (count & shares)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of appellations of origin (AOs) and GIs in force via the Lisbon System and shares by origin country/party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report growth rates (e.g., 'AOs and GIs in force via Lisbon System grew by 3.4% in 2021 to reach 1,052') and country shares (e.g., France, Italy, EU, Czech Republic, Iran). Note accession/party changes affect totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting/aggregation rule for regional systems (double-count minimization)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a regional system covers multiple member states, GIs in force via that regional system are counted once rather than multiple times across member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aggregation approach is explicitly used for the EU regional system to minimize double counting across member states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special national/regional reporting rules / exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Country-specific rules affecting counts (examples provided: Switzerland, UK, US).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switzerland: no registration requirement for sui generis protection; only denominations subject to registration/recognition/court decision or special legislation are counted under national systems. UK: new UK GI scheme after Brexit includes all GIs directly registered by the EU prior to Dec 31, 2022. US: protects GIs through trademark system as certification/collective marks and via complementary Federal Alcohol Administration Act for wines and spirits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness caveat for GI statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The GIs in force data reported are partial and incomplete and therefore ought to be interpreted with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questionnaire requested info on GIs protected through designated categories; many countries did not provide statistics on GIs protected via trademark system or international agreements. Absence of data may reflect reporting difficulty rather than absence of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of EU data to income groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: European Union data are allocated to the high‑income group for classification purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: most EU member states are high‑income; this is a policy choice for grouping in cross‑country comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI data source documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Source of GI data is the WIPO Statistics Database and country questionnaire responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure metadata records which legal means category and whether counts include foreign GIs, Lisbon System entries, and how regional counts were treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing industry survey scope (inclusion criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of the publishing industry survey is limited to (a) the trade and educational sectors and (b) those published materials issued with an ISBN, a DOI or any other book identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data were drawn from national publishers' associations and copyright authorities; note limitations in representativeness due to varying NPA coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing industry revenue (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total sales and licensing revenue for the publishing industry (typically presented in USD million) for the specified sectors and year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revenue can be reported at market value (retail prices) or net revenue; some countries report print only while omitting digital components—document reporting basis for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing revenue by format (print vs digital/audio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of publishing industry revenue by format: print and digital/audio formats (digital/audio may be combined in reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report share of digital/audio; note some countries only report print; format definitions must be consistent across respondents when comparing shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing revenue by destination (domestic vs foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share (and absolute amounts) of publishing revenue generated from domestic markets vs foreign markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both percentage share and absolute USD where possible; example: UK generated 40.7% of total revenue from foreign markets in 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing revenue by sales channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of revenue by sales channel: brick and mortar, online (including digital sales), and other channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define 'online' to include digital sales; reporting basis (market value vs net) can affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's books revenue (metric and share)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total revenue generated from children's books and the share of children's books revenue within trade sector revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute USD and percent of trade sector; data availability varies across countries (example totals and country-specific shares provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of titles published (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of titles published in a year covering the trade and educational sectors (by format where available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report by sector and format where possible; some countries report print only. Note double counting if multiple ISBNs used for different formats/editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles published by format (print, digital, audio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of titles published broken down by format (print, digital, audio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percentage shares; digital/audio shares vary widely across countries (e.g., Brazil 65.9% digital/audio share of titles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal deposit obligation (definition and minimum copies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal deposit is a statutory obligation requiring publishers to deposit a certain number of copies of published documents at a recognized repository; ordinarily at least two copies are required, although this varies across countries/territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some countries require deposit only for printed books; others require digital publications; digitization has affected coverage. When comparing, document whether e‑books/digital items are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories in legal deposits statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal deposits survey covers four categories of deposit: (a) books, (b) music sheets and music audio files, (c) films and videos, and (d) periodicals (journals, e‑series, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that in some countries audiovisual or other items may be collected by different agencies; specify which national agency provided each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rules and format coverage for legal deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of deposited items depend on national rules and data collection practices (digital vs physical, whether digitized items are counted), causing cross‑country comparability issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Denmark reports almost all film/video deposits in digital format; some countries report physical format only — document format coverage when using comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISBN registrations (metrics and interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of ISBN registrations (lifetime and annual) as an indicator of publishing output and market size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISBN system has a three‑tier administrative structure (International ISBN Agency, national/regional agencies, publishers). Publishers assign unique ISBNs to publications; be aware of double counting because different formats/editions get separate ISBNs. Alternative identifiers (ASIN, DOI) may be used and affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing data source and comparability caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing industry data are drawn from multiple surveys (publishing industry survey, legal deposits survey, ISBN registrations) and compiled to provide an overview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because data come from different sources and respondent coverage varies (NPAs, national repositories, ISBN agencies), exercise caution in cross‑country comparisons; document whether reported values are print‑only, include digital, or are market value vs net.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical indicator catalogue (F1–F19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined list of statistical tables/figures used in the chapter: F1 Publishing industry revenue; F2 Distribution by format; F3 Distribution by destination; F4 Distribution by sales channel; F5 Children's books revenue; F6 Share of children's books; F7 Number of titles published; F8 Titles by format; F9 Number of children's titles; F10 Share of children's books; F11 Number of books deposited at top repositories; F12 Distribution of deposited books by format; F13 Total music deposits; F14 Distribution of music deposits; F15 Films/videos deposited; F16–F19 detailed tables for revenue, titles, deposits, ISBNs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these named indicators/tables as the standard outputs for reporting and cross‑country comparison; ensure accompanying metadata documents definitions and any country‑specific deviations.
